standard_prerequisites.name: Well-founded relation and accessibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: A relation < on A is well-founded when every a:A is accessible, written acc(a); acc(a) is the type of witnesses that all predecessors of a are accessible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis of the statement and the object the proof recurses on.

standard_prerequisites.name: Power set
standard_prerequisites.statement: power B is the type B->prop, the type of subsets of the set B.
standard_prerequisites.use: The recursion datum g is a function power B -> B.

standard_prerequisites.name: Image of a subset
standard_prerequisites.statement: setof{ f(a') | a'<a } is the subset of B consisting of the values of f on the predecessors of a.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the argument at which g is evaluated in the recursion equation.

core_obligations: Define by recursion on accessibility a function fbar taking a:A and s:acc(a) to an element of B, so that fbar(a,s) = g(setof{ fbar(a',s(a')) | a'<a }) (source lines 1020-1025).
Use that < is well-founded to obtain a function w:prod_{a:A} acc(a) (source line 1027).
Set f(a) = fbar(a,w(a)) and check that the recursion equation holds, which is immediate from the definition of fbar (source line 1028).

proof_roadmap.step: Recurse on the accessibility witness and define fbar by g applied to the image of its own values on the predecessors.
Discharge the accessibility hypothesis with the well-foundedness of < and define f(a) from fbar and w.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Lemma 10.3.7 at source lines 1009-1016: given a set B, a function g from the power set of B to B and a well-founded relation < on A, there is f:A->B with f(a)=g(setof{ f(a') | a'<a }) for every a:A. The author's proof (source lines 1019-1029) is short but its whole content is a single careful recursion: one has to recurse on the accessibility witness rather than on the element of A, supplying at each step not only the values fbar(a',s(a')) but the witnesses s(a') for the predecessors, and only then discharge the accessibility hypothesis through the well-foundedness of < to obtain a genuine function on A. The statement records the recursion equation but neither the accessibility recursion nor the passage from fbar to f.
